description: Notwithstanding the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking, re-enacting or modifying that Order), the A1-A3, D1, D2 ‘commercial units’ hereby approved shall be used for uses falling within these use classes and for no other purposes of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order.
reason: To ensure that the development hereby permitted contributes positively to the vision for Lewisham Town Centre and the objectives for the Loampit Vale Policy Area as required by Policies LTC2 and LTC4 in the Lewisham Town Centre Local Plan (February 2014).

name: Condition 5: Shop Front Design
description: (a) Future shop front applications shall be in accordance with the ‘Lewisham Retail Park Shop Front Design Guide’ (set out in Section 7.12 in Design and Access Statement) (b) No development shall commence above 2nd floor level on site until plans and sectional details at a scale of 1:10 or 1:20 showing the proposed frontages to the commercial units have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. (c) The development shall be constructed in full accordance with the approved details.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied with the details of the proposal and to accord with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) DM Policy 19 Shop fronts, signs and hoardings.

name: Condition 6: Commercial Opening Hours
description: The A1-A3, D1, D2 ‘commercial units’ hereby approved shall not be used other than between the hours of 07.00 and 23.00 on any day of the week.
reason: In order to safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area generally and to comply with DM Policy 26 Noise and Vibration and DM Policy 32 Housing design, layout and space standards of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 7: Noise break-out
description: No music, amplified sound system or other form of loud noise (such as singing or chanting) shall be used or generated which is audible outside any of the A1-A3, D1, D2 ‘commercial units’ hereby approved.
reason: To safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area generally and to comply with DM Policy 26 Noise and Vibration and DM Policy 32 Housing design, layout and space standards of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 8: Ventilation
description: (a)The specification of the appearance of and the equipment comprising a ventilation system which shall include measures to alleviate noise, vibration, fumes and odours (and incorporating active carbon filters, silencers and anti-vibration mountings where necessary) in respect of any A3 use of a Commercial Unit shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to first occupation of any Commercial Unit for A3 purposes. (b) No non-residential unit shall be first occupied for A3 purposes until the ventilation systems as approved under part (a) of this condition has been installed in that Commercial Unit in accordance with the plans and specification approved under the said part (a) and such ventilation systems shall thereafter be permanently retained and maintained in accordance with the approved specification.
reason: To safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area generally and to comply with Policy 17 Restaurants and cafes (A3 uses) and drinking establishments (A4 uses) of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 9: Screens to Amenity Space
description: (a) Prior to occupation of any residential dwelling, full details of proposed screens around the edge of to the approved podium level garden and communal amenity area on Level 19 of Building A shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. (b) The approved screens for the podium garden shall be implemented before any residential dwelling is first occupied. (c) The approved screens for the amenity area on Building A shall be implemented before any residential dwelling in Building A is first occupied. (d) The approved screens shall be maintained thereafter
reason: In order to protect the amenities of the future occupiers of the relevant residential dwellings.

name: Condition 10: Podium Garden Landscaping
description: (a) Notwithstanding the generality of the details shown on Drawing A2605 212 R3, full details of the proposed hard and soft landscaping of the podium garden space hereby permitted shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA within 6 months of commencement of development above slab level. (b) The approved hard and soft landscaping shall be implemented and thereafter retained in accordance with the approved details.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied as to the details of the proposal and to comply with Core Strategy Policy 12 Open space and environmental assets, Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011), and DM Policy 25 Landscaping and trees and DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 11: Garden Spaces and Public Realm Landscaped Areas
description: Notwithstanding the generality of the details shown on Drawing A2605 210 R3, full details of the proposed hard and soft landscaping of the private garden spaces and public realm areas along Thurston Road hereby permitted shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority within 6 months of commencement of development above slab level. The approved hard and soft landscaping shall be implemented and thereafter retained in accordance with the approved details.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied as to the details of the proposal and to safeguard the provision of a Bakerloo Line Extension in accordance with Core Strategy Policy 12 Open space and environmental assets, Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011), and DM Policy 25 Landscaping and trees, DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) and Policies 6.1 and 6.2 of the London Plan 2016.

name: Condition 12: Open Space Management and Maintenance Plan
description: (a) An Open Space Management & Maintenance Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority at the same time as the Podium Garden Landscaping and Public Realm Landscaped Areas are submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority within 6 months of commencement of development above slab level. These shall include management & maintenance and responsibilities for all communal play spaces/amenity spaces and all publicly accessible open spaces. (b) Once provided, these spaces shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved Plan.
reason: To ensure that the podium garden and public realm landscaping areas are adequately managed in accordance with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and DM Policy 25 Landscaping and trees in the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 13: External Materials - Buildings
description: Buildings A to G shall be finished in those materials identified on Drawings A2605 500 R1, A2605 520 R2, A2605 530 R1, A2605 540 R1, A2605 550 R1 and A2605 570 R1 and page 25 of the Design and Access Statement Addendum (17 March 2017) and the Building Materials Outline Specification dated 06 October 2016 unless minor variations are otherwise approved in writing by the local planning authority.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied as to the external appearance of the proposal in accordance with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) and Policies 7.4 Local character and 7.6 Architecture of the London Plan 2016.

name: Condition 14: External Materials - Buildings (Details and Samples)
description: No development shall commence on site until a detailed schedule, drawings and samples of the following have been submitted to and approved in by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. (i) 1m x 1m sample panel to be constructed on site each proposed brick type for all buildings. Details of mortar are to be provided. The brick type shall accord with the materials as set out in the Building Materials Outline Specification dated 06 October 2016. (ii) 1m x 1m sample panels of bricks. Details of mortar are to be provided. (iii) Samples of all windows, including joinery and fixing. (iv) All glazed and metal balustrade for balconies including details of fixing and handrails where applicable. (v) Samples of cladding to all balconies, including soffit finish and provision to handle rainwater. (vi) Samples of perforated metal sheets at ground and first floor along Thurston Road Boundary treatment details of Thurston Road frontage. (vii) Detailed elevation and section drawings at 1:5 of the grills to the ground floor car parking areas and Town House storage areas.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied as to the external appearance of the proposal in accordance with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) and Policies 7.4 Local character and 7.6 Architecture of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 15: Secure by Design
description: No part of the development hereby approved shall be first occupied until certification that the development has achieved Secure by Design accreditation has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
reason: To ensure that the local planning authority may be satisfied that the proposal reduces opportunities for criminal behaviour and makes a positive contribution to a sense of security and to comply with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) and Policy 7.3 Designing out crime of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 16: Satellite Dishes
description: Notwithstanding the Provisions of Article 4 (1) and part 25 of Schedule 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015, no satellite antenna shall be erected or installed on the building hereby approved. The proposed development shall have a central dish or aerial system for receiving all broadcasts for the residential units created: details of such a scheme shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority prior to the occupation of the property, and the approved scheme shall be implemented and permanently retained thereafter.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied with the details of the proposal and to accord with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 17: Accessible Housing
description: (a) The detailed design for each dwelling hereby approved shall meet the required standard of the Approved Document M of the Building Regulations (2015) as specified in the schedule below: Unit reference number Approved Document M Dwelling type (2015) Access Requirement List all Market tenure M4(3)(2)(a) Wheelchair user wheelchair units: (adaptable) B-2-2, B-2-5, B-3-2, B-3-5, B-4-2, B-4-5, B-5-2, B-5-5, B-6-2, B-6-5, B-7-6, B-8-6, B-9-6, B-10-6, B-11-7, B-12-6, B-13-6, B-14-6, C-2-1, C-2-2, C-7-1, C-8-1, D-2-5, D-3-7, D-4-7, D-5-7, D-6-7, E-2-4, E-3-4, E-4-4, E-5-4, E-6-4 and E-7-4. List all Social Rented M4(3)(2)(b) Wheelchair user (on wheelchair units: completion) F-2-1, F-2-7, F-3-1, F-3-7, F-4-1, F-4-7, F-5-1, F-5-7, F-6-1, F-6-7, F-7-1, F-7-7, F-8-6, F-9-6, F10-6 and F-11-6. List all Shared Ownership M4(3)(2)(a) Wheelchair user wheelchair units: F-12-6, (adaptable) F-13-6, F-14-6, F-15-6 and F-16-6. All other units M4(2) Accessible and (b) No development shall commence above ground level until written confirmation from the appointed building control body has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority to demonstrate compliance with part (a). (c) The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details approved under part (b).
reason: To ensure that there is an adequate supply of wheelchair accessible housing in the Borough in accordance with Policy 1 Housing provision, mix and affordability and Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and DM Policy 32 Housing design, layout and space standards of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 18: Air Quality
description: (a) The boilers to be provided for space heating and domestic hot water shall have ‘ultra-low’ dry NOx emissions not exceeding 40 mg/kWh. (b) The CHP unit to be provided shall comply with the emissions standards for ‘Band B’ as set out in the Mayor of London’s Sustainable Design and Construction SPG (2014). (c) Air intake points for the ventilation of dwellings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority before any dwelling is first occupied. Intake points shall thereafter be implemented and maintained in the approved locations.
reason: To prevent an increase in local problems of air quality within an Air Quality Management Areas (AQMAs) as required by London Plan Policy 7.14 and DM Policy 28.

name: Condition 19: Protection Against External Noise - Buildings
description: (a) (i) The residential units herby approved shall be designed so as to provide sound insulation against external noise and vibration, to achieve levels not exceeding 30dB LAeq (night) and 45dB LAmax for bedrooms, 35dB LAeq (day) for other habitable rooms, with windows shut and other means of ventilation provided; (a) (ii) The evaluation of human exposure to vibration within the buildings shall not exceed the vibration dose values criteria ‘Low probability of adverse comment’ as defined BS6472. (b) Development of residential units in any Block shall not commence until details of a sound and vibration insulation scheme complying with part (a)(i), (ii)and (iii) of this condition and a Mechanical Ventilation and Heat Recovery (MVHR) system for that Block have been submitted to an approved in writing by the local planning authority. (c) The residential units in a particular Block shall not be occupied until the sound and vibration insulation scheme and MVHR system approved pursuant to part (b) of this condition for that Block has been implemented in its entirety. Thereafter, the sound and vibration insulation scheme shall be permanently maintained in accordance with the approved details.
reason: To safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of the proposed dwellings and to comply with DM Policy 26 Noise and vibration, DM Policy 32 Housing design, layout and space standards of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 20: Protection Against External Noise - Amenity Spaces
description: The design and specification of the screens required to the podium level garden and all communal amenity areas hereby approved shall ensure that noise levels in these spaces shall not exceed 55dB LAEQT.
reason: To safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of the proposed dwellings and to comply with DM Policy 26 Noise and vibration, DM Policy 32 Housing design, layout and space standards of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 21: Fixed Plant Noise Control
description: (a) The rating level of the noise emitted from fixed plant on the site shall be 5dB below the existing background level at any time. The noise levels shall be determined at the façade of any noise sensitive property. The measurements and assessments shall be made according to BS4142:2014. (b)Other than demolition, site clearance and ground works, development shall not commence until details of a scheme complying with part (a) of this condition have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. (c) The development shall not be occupied until the scheme approved pursuant to part (b) of this condition has been implemented in its entirety. The scheme as approved shall be permanently retained thereafter.
reason: To safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of the proposed dwellings and to comply with DM Policy 26 Noise and vibration, DM Policy 32 Housing design, layout and space standards of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 22: External Lighting
description: Prior to first occupation of the development, a scheme for any external lighting that is to be installed at the site, including measures to prevent light spillage, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority and such details shall include evidence to demonstrate that the proposed lighting is the minimum needed for security and working purposes and that the proposals minimise pollution from glare and spillage, following the Institute of Lighting Engineer’s guidance and shall not exceed 2 lux at any window of a habitable room. Any such approved external lighting shall be installed in accordance with the scheme approved under part (a) of this condition and shall thereafter only be retained in accordance with the scheme approved under the said part (a).
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied that the lighting is installed and maintained in a manner which will minimise possible light pollution to the night sky and neighbouring properties and to comply with DM Policy 27 Lighting of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 23: Car Parking Spaces, Disabled Car Parking Spaces and Electric Vehicle Charging Points
description: Points (a) Prior to first occupation of the development, plans shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local authority showing the location of the general car parking bays (28 for non-residential uses), disabled car parking bays (54 for the residential dwellings and 3 for non-residential uses) and electric vehicle charging points (11 for the residential dwellings with passive provision for a further 11 spaces for the residential dwellings and 3 for the non-residential uses with passive provision for a further 3-4 spaces for the non-residential uses). (b) The approved parking arrangements shall be implemented and made ready for use prior to the first occupation of the development.
reason: To reduce pollution emissions in an Area Quality Management Area in accordance with Policy 6.13 and 7.14 of the London Plan (March 2016), and DM Policy 29 Car parking of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 24: Cycle Parking Spaces
description: (a) Prior to first occupation of the development, plans shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local authority identifying the location and details of the long and short stay residential (minimum 880 long-stay and 13 short-stay) and retail cycle parking (minimum 25 long-stay and 109 short-stay) and adapted cycle parking spaces and the locations of showers and lockers for employees of the retail units arriving by bicycle. (b) The approved parking arrangements shall be implemented and made ready for use prior to the first occupation of the development.
reason: To accord with Policy 14 Sustainable movement and transport in the Lewisham Core Strategy (June 2011), Policy 6.13 of the London Plan (March 2016) and DM Policy 29 section 6 of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 25: Parking Managment Plan
description: (a) Prior to the first occupation of the development, a Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local authority. The Management Plan shall include details of: (i) Allocation and management of car, motorcycle and cycle parking spaces within the development (iii) Measures taken to control the length of stay within the commercial car parking area (with customers of businesses in the development being able to park their car in one of the customer car parking spaces for up to 2 hours at no charge. (b) The car and cycle parking spaces shall only be operated in accordance with an approved Parking Management Plan
reason: To manage car and cycle parking in accordance with London Plan Policy 6.13 and DM Policy 29 Car parking of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) and to reduce pollution emissions in an Area Quality Management Area in accordance with Policy 7.14 Improving air quality in the London Plan (July 2011).

name: Condition 26: Delivery and Servicing Managment Plan
description: Prior to the first occupation of the development, a Delivery and Servicing Management Plan, including the proposed location of delivery and service areas, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local authority, to include details of how deliveries and servicing will be effectively managed at the development bays and any required changes to parking restrictions surrounding the development.
reason: In order to ensure satisfactory vehicle management and to comply with Policy 14 Sustainable movement and transport of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and Policy 6.3 of the London Plan (March 2016).

name: Condition 27: Restriction of Size of Vehicles Servicing the Development
description: No vehicle entering the development shall have a length greater than 10.00 metres, and width greater than 2.50 metres and a height greater than 3.645 metres.
reason: In the interests of highway safety and to ensure all vehicles entering the development can manoeuvre safely within the development and exit in forward gear.

name: Condition 28: Visibility Splays
description: Prior to the first occupation of the development, plans shall be submitted to and approving in writing by the local authority to show details of vehicle and pedestrian visibility splays at the proposed vehicular accesses and shall be subsequently maintained clear of any obstruction over 0.6 metres above footway level. For the avoidance of doubt, vehicle splays should be a minimum of 2.4 by 43.0 metres and pedestrian intervisibliity splays should be a minimum of 2.0 by 2.0 metres
reason: In the interests of highway safety

name: Condition 29: Safeguarding Bakerloo Line Extension
description: Prior to the commencement of the development a method statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local authority to demonstrate to the local planning authority’s satisfaction that detailed arrangements for the construction and operation of the development hereby permitted shall not impede the future construction and operation of a Bakerloo Line Extension to and through Lewisham Town Centre.
reason: To safeguard the provision of a Bakerloo Line Extension and accord with Policy 14 Sustainable movement and transport in the Lewisham Core Strategy (June 2011) Policies 6.1 and 6.2 of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 30: DLR Radio Communications
description: (a) A ‘pre’ and ‘post development Radio Communications Survey Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, in consultation with Transport for London, within 3 months of completion of development. The Report shall set out an assessment of the level of any impact the development has on the strength of DLR radio signals and identify any necessary mitigation measures (including signal boosters). (b) Any identified necessary mitigation measures shall be implemented within 6 months of the Report being approved.
reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not compromise the safe and effective operation of the DLRL network.

name: Condition 31: Highway Mitigation/ Public Realm
description: No development shall commence until such time as the developer has entered into a Highways Agreement with the Highway Authority to secure the implementation of following highway mitigation works: (a) Modifications to waiting and loading and car parking restrictions to facilitate scheme, including relocation of bus stand on Jerrard Street and converting Red Route parking bay on Jerrard Street to a loading bay; (b) Provision of on-street cycle parking spaces; (c) Provision of 2 x on-street car club parking bays; (d) Tying in new site boundary with existing public highway and creation of two new accesses; (e) Removal of redundant vehicle accesses and replacement with footway/cycleway as appropriate (5 redundant cross overs as shown on Drawing 15.545.110 October 2016); (f) Removal and relocation of existing signalling junction boxes, telephone box and air monitoring equipment within Loampit Vale public highway (as shown on Drawing 15.545.110 October 2016); (g) Improvement works to the footways on Loampit Vale, Jerrard Street and Thurston Road, including setting back development boundaries to achieve footway widths to a minimum of 8 metres on the Loampit Vale frontage (taking account of TfL proposals for carriageway widening) and minimum of 6 metres on the Jerrard Street and Thurston Road frontages; (h) Adoption by TfL of Loampit Vale footway up to the approved new back of highway; (i) Stopping up of redundant highway land on Loampit Vale; and (j) Improved pedestrian/cycle crossing point at Jerrard Street/Thurston Road junction.
reason: To ensure an acceptable standard of development in accordance with Policies DM Policy 35 Public realm of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) and Policies LTC18 Public realm and LTC21 Sustainable transport of the Lewisham Town Centre Local Plan (February 2014).

name: Condition 32: Flood Risk
description: The ground floor of the non-residential units and residential lobby and storage areas hereby approved shall incorporate ‘flood resilient’ features as set out in the Lewisham Retail Park Flood Risk Assessment Revision 01.
reason: To ensure that development is resilient to flooding in accordance with Policies 5.12 Flood risk management and 5.13 Sustainable drainage in the London Plan (2016) and Objective 6: Flood risk reduction and water management and Core Strategy Policy 10: Managing and reducing the risk of flooding (2011).

name: Condition 33: Drainage
description: The Foul and Surface Water Drainage Strategy (Ref 034682 dated 15 July 2016) shall be implemented in full before any residential dwelling hereby approved is first occupied. No drainage systems for the infiltration of surface water drainage in to the ground are permitted other than with the express written consent of the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with the Environment Agency, which may be given for those parts of the site where it has been demonstrated that there is no resultant unacceptable risk to controlled waters. Any such approved drainage systems shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
reason: To prevent the increased risk of flooding, to improve water quality and to ensure that drainage does not present a contamination risk to groundwater in accordance with Policies 5.12 Flood risk management and 5.13 Sustainable drainage in the London Plan (2016) and Objective 6: Flood risk reduction and water management and Core Strategy Policy 10: Managing and reducing the risk of flooding (2011) and to comply with Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) DM Policy 28 Contaminated land.

name: Condition 34: Living Roofs
description: (a)Within 6 months of commencement of development above slab level, details of the biodiversity living roof which shall allow for a substrate depth of 150 mm and shall be designed to support a water load of 12litres/m2 (=12kg/m2) and a soil load of 150mm depth minimum (circa 225kg/m2) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. (b) The biodiversity living roof shall be laid out in accordance with Plan no. A2605 234 R1 approved under Condition 2 and provided in accordance with the details approved under part (a) of this condition and such biodiversity living roof shall thereafter be permanently retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details. (c)The biodiversity living roof shall not be used as an amenity or sitting out space of any kind whatsoever and shall only be used in the case of essential maintenance or repair, or escape in case of emergency.
reason: To comply with Policies 5.10 Urban greening, 5.11 Green roofs and development site environs, 5.12 Flood risk management, 5.13 Sustainable Drainage and 7.19 Biodiversity and access to nature conservation in the London Plan (2016), Policy 10 managing and reducing flood risk and Policy 12 Open space and environmental assets of the Core Strategy (June 2011), and DM Policy 24 Biodiversity, living roofs and artificial playing pitches of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 35: Ecology
description: (a) Prior to above ground works, a Habitat Creation Management Plan (BCMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and include (i) Planting of trees and shrubs at podium level, covering a variety of species, including those of benefit to wildlife; (ii) The provision of ‘wild’ and diverse areas planted with a range of native wildflower species attractive to invertebrates; (iii)Installation of 10 bird boxes of various sizes to cover a range of local species; and (iv) Installation of peregrine nest box on top of Building A. (b) Approved details are to be implemented and maintained as approved.
reason: To comply with Policy 7.19 Biodiversity and access to nature conservation in the London Plan (2016), Policy 12 Open space and environmental assets of the Core Strategy (June 2011), and DM Policy 24 Biodiversity, living roofs and artificial playing pitches and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 36: Contaminated Land
description: (a) No development (including demolition of existing buildings and structures, except where prior agreement with the Council for site investigation enabling works has been received) shall commence until: - (i) A desk top study and site assessment to survey and characterise the nature and extent of contamination and its effect (whether on or off-site) and a conceptual site model have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority in consultation with the Environment Agency. (ii) A site investigation report to characterise and risk assess the site which shall include the gas, hydrological and contamination status, specifying rationale; and recommendations for treatment for contamination encountered (whether by remedial works or not) has been submitted, (including subsequent correspondences as being necessary or desirable for the remediation of the site) to and approved in writing by the Council, in consultation with the Environment Agency. (b) The remediation scheme approved under Part (a) shall be implemented in full. (c) If during any works on the site, contamination is encountered which has not previously been identified (“the new contamination”) the Council shall be notified immediately and the terms of paragraph (a), shall apply to the new contamination. No further works shall take place on that part of the site or adjacent areas affected, until the requirements of paragraph (a) have been complied with in relation to the new contamination. (d) The development shall not be occupied until a closure report for the development has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Council, in consultation with the Environment Agency. This shall include verification of all measures, or treatments as required in (Section (a) i & ii) and relevant correspondence (including other regulating authorities and stakeholders involved with the remediation works) to verify compliance requirements, necessary for the remediation of the site have been implemented in full. (d) The closure report shall include verification details of both the remediation and post-remediation sampling/works, carried out (including waste materials removed from the site); and before placement of any soil/materials is undertaken on site, all imported or reused soil material must conform to current soil quality requirements as agreed by the authority. Inherent to the above, is the provision of any required documentation, certification and monitoring, to facilitate condition requirements.
reason: To ensure that the local planning authority may be satisfied that potential site contamination is identified and remedied in view of the historical use(s) of the site, which may have included industrial processes and for the protection of controlled waters and to comply with Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) DM Policy 28 Contaminated land.

name: Condition 37: Energy and Efficiency - New Homes
description: The residential units hereby approved shall achieve the following energy efficiency and water efficiency standards: i) Energy efficiency - a 37.2% improvement in the Dwelling Emission Rate over the Target Emission Rate as defined in Part L1A of the 2010 Building Regulations (as amended). (ii) Water efficiency - The sanitary fittings within each residential dwelling shall include low water use WCs, shower taps, baths and (where installed by the developer) white goods to comply with an average household water consumption of less than 105 litres/person/day.
reason: To comply with Policies 5.1 Climate change and mitigation, 5.2 Minimising carbon dioxide emissions, 5.3 Sustainable design and construction, 5.7 Renewable energy, 5.15 Water use and supplies in the London Plan (2016) and Core Strategy Policy 7 Climate change and adapting to the effects, Core Strategy Policy 8 Sustainable design and construction and energy efficiency (2011).

name: Condition 38: BREEAM
description: (a) The buildings hereby approved shall achieve a minimum BREEAM Rating of ‘Excellent’. (b) No development shall commence until a Design Stage Certificate for each building (prepared by a Building Research Establishment qualified Assessor) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority to demonstrate compliance with part (a). (c) Within 3 months of occupation of any of the buildings, evidence shall be submitted in the form of a Post Construction Certificate (prepared by a Building Research Establishment qualified Assessor) to demonstrate full compliance with part (a) for that specific building.
reason: To comply with Policies 5.1 Climate change and mitigation, 5.2 Minimising carbon dioxide emissions, 5.3 Sustainable design and construction, 5.7 Renewable energy, 5.15 Water use and supplies in the London Plan (2016) and Core Strategy Policy 7 Climate change and adapting to the effects, Core Strategy Policy 8 Sustainable design and construction and energy efficiency (2011).

name: Condition 39: Archaeology
description: (a) No development other than demolition to existing ground level shall take place until the applicant (or their heirs and successors in title) has secured the implementation of a programme of archaeological evaluation site work in accordance with a Written Scheme of Investigation which has been submitted by the applicant and approved by the local planning authority in writing. (b) Under Part (a), the applicant (or their heirs and successors in title) shall implement a programme of archaeological evaluation in accordance with a Written Scheme of Investigation. (c) A report of the evaluation results will be submitted for approval by the local planning authority which will be given in writing. (d) Dependent upon the results presented under Part (c), no development other than demolition to existing ground level shall take place until the applicant (or their heirs and successors in title) has secured the implementation of a programme of archaeological mitigation site work in accordance with a Written Scheme of Investigation which has been submitted by the applicant and approved by the local planning authority in writing. (e) Under Part (d), the applicant (or their heirs and successors in title) shall implement a programme of archaeological mitigation in accordance with a Written Scheme of Investigation. (f) The site investigation and post-investigation assessment will be completed prior to one year post the completion date of the development as defined by the borough building regulation officer, in accordance with the programme set out in the Written Scheme of Investigation approved under Parts (a) and (d), and the provision for post investigation assessment, analysis, of the results and archive deposition has been secured.
reason: To conserve, protect and enhancement the archaeological heritage of Lewisham in accordance with Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) DM Policy 37 Non-designated heritage assets including locally listed buildings, areas of special local character and areas of archaeological interest.

name: Condition 40: Site Waste Management Plan
description: Demolition and construction activities shall be carried out in accordance with the Lewisham Retail Park Site Waste Management Plan (034682, 15 July 2016).
reason: To minimise the generation of and increase recovery of demolition and construction waste and to comply with Policy 5.18 Construction, excavation and demolition waste of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 41: Construction Environment Management Plan
description: (a) Development shall not commence until such time as a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The plan shall cover: - (i) Dust mitigation measures in the form of a Dust Management Plan and include communications, site management and monitoring arrangements specified in section 10.4.3 of the Environmental Statement. (ii) The location and operation of plant and wheel washing facilities (iii) Details of best practical measures to be employed to mitigate noise and vibration arising out of the construction process (iv) Security Management (to minimise risks to unauthorised personnel). (v) Details of the training of site operatives to follow any Environmental Management Plan requirements (vi) Timing and methodology for removal of trees and buildings (minimising impact on any nesting birds) (vii) Control of removal of cotoneaster (‘Coral Beauty’) (viii) Pollution of water/ flood risk (ix) Unexploded Ordnance survey (b) No works shall be carried out other than in accordance with the Construction Management Plan as approved under part (a) of this condition
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied that the demolition and construction process is carried out in a manner which will minimise possible noise, disturbance and pollution to neighbouring properties and to comply with Policy 5.3 Sustainable design and construction, Policy 6.3 Assessing effects of development on transport capacity and Policy 7.14 Improving air quality of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 42: Piling
description: (a) No piling or any other foundation designs using penetrative methods shall take place, other than with the prior written approval of the local planning authority, following consultation with Thames Water and the Environment Agency. (b) Details of any such operations referred to in part (a) of this condition must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to commencement of any piling works and such details shall include details of the relevant penetrative methods. (c) Any such operations referred to in part (a) of this condition shall be carried out only in accordance with the details approved under part (b) of this condition.
reason: To prevent pollution of controlled waters and to comply with Core Strategy (2011) Policy 11 River and waterways network and Development Management Local Plan (November 2014) DM Policy 28 Contaminated land.

name: Condition 43: Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM)
description: An inventory of all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) shall be kept on-site and registered on http://nrmm.London/ showing the emission limits for all equipment and shall be made available to Local Planning Authority offices if required. All NRMM of net power between 37kW and 560kW will be required to meet Stage IIIA of EU Directive 97/68/EC.’
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied that the demolition and construction process is carried out in a manner which will minimise possible noise, disturbance and pollution to neighbouring properties and to comply with Policy 5.3 Sustainable design and construction, Policy 6.3 Assessing effects of development on transport capacity and Policy 7.14 Improving air quality of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 44: Construction Logistics Plan
description: (a) No development shall commence on site until an updated Construction Logistics Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall demonstrate the following: - · Rationalise travel and traffic routes to and from the site. · Provide full details of the number and time of construction vehicle trips to the site with the intention and aim of reducing the impact of construction vehicle activity on road traffic and residential amenity by · Minimising trips to and from the site between 08.00 and 09.00 and 15.00 and 18.00 during Prendergast Vale School term times and 08.00 and 09.00 and 17.00 and 18.00 during school holidays; · Traffic marshalling and off/on site holding areas; and · Taking account of delivery times of any other construction sites within 500m of the site which are due to be active at the same time. · Measures to deal with safe pedestrian movement. · Full details of how the cycle and pedestrian networks on Thurston Road and at the Thurston Road/Jerrard Street junction are to be maintained · Construction staging and how this will impact on access/egress arrangements and avoid adverse impact on bus operations on Jerrard Street and Thurston Road. (b) The measures specified in the approved details shall be implemented prior to commencement of development and shall be adhered to during the period of construction.
reason: In order to ensure satisfactory vehicle management and to comply with Policy 14 Sustainable movement and transport of the Core Strategy (2011), and Policy 5.3 Sustainable design and construction, Policy 6.3 Assessing effects of development on transport capacity and Policy 7.14 Improving air quality of the London Plan (2016).

name: Condition 45: Construction - Deliveries and Hours of Working
description: No work, other than vehicle movements to and from the site in accordance with an approved Construction Logistics Management Plan, shall take place on the site other than between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 on Mondays to Fridays and 08.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays and not at all on Sundays or Public Holidays.
reason: In order to ensure satisfactory vehicle management and to comply with Policy 14 Sustainable movement and transport of the Core Strategy (June 2011).

name: Condition 46: Tree Protection
description: No development shall commence until a Tree Protection Plan (TPP) in respect of the existing trees to be retained along Loampit Vale and Thurston Road has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The TPP shall follow the recommendations set out in BS 5837:2012 (Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations). The TPP shall also clearly indicate on a dimensioned plan superimposed on the building layout plan and in a written schedule details of the location and form of protective barriers to form a construction exclusion zone, the extent and type of ground protection measures, and any additional measures needed to protect vulnerable sections of trees and their root protection areas where construction activity cannot be fully or permanently excluded.
reason: To safeguard the health and safety of trees during building operations and the visual amenities of the area generally and to comply with Policy 12 Open space and environmental assets of the Core Strategy (June 2011), and DM Policy 25 Landscaping and trees and DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 47: External Pipework
description: Notwithstanding the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking, re-enacting or modifying that Order), no plumbing or pipes, including rainwater pipes, shall be fixed on the external facades of any building hereby approved.
reason: In order that the local planning authority may be satisfied with the details of the proposal and to accord with Policy 15 High quality design for Lewisham of the Core Strategy (June 2011) and DM Policy 30 Urban design and local character of the Development Management Local Plan (November 2014).

name: Condition 1
description: The development hereby permitted shall only be carried out in all respects in accordance with proposals contained in the application and the plans hereby approved or as shall have been otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in full accordance with the plans and particulars hereby approved.

name: Condition 2
description: Details of the (i) Access, (ii) Appearance, (iii) Landscaping, (iv) Layout and (v) Scale (as defined by the Town and Country Planning (General Development Procedure) Order 1995 (as amended) (hereinafter called "the Reserved Matters") for each phase of development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before each phase of development commences. Each phase of development shall be carried in accordance with the Reserved Matters as approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the Local Authority is satisfied with the details of the proposed development.

name: Condition 3
description: Applications for approval of the Reserved Matters of the first phase of development shall be made to the Local Planning Authority not later than THREE years from the date of this permission. Applications for approval of the Reserve Matters of the final phase of development shall be made to the Local Planning Authority not later than TEN years from the date of this permission. The first phase and final phase of the development hereby permitted shall begin not later than TWO years from the date of approval of the last of the reserved matters to be approved, or, in the case of approval on different dates, the final approval of the last such matter to be approved.
reason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

name: Condition 4
description: Prior to commencement of development a Phasing Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The phasing of the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved phasing plan, unless an alternative phasing plan is first submitted to the Local Planning Authority with an assessment of any effects, including any different impacts on the environment, and that alternative plan and assessment is approved by the Local Planning Authority pursuant to this condition.
reason: To ensure that the proposed development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission and scheme of works, and to avoid any detriment to the comprehensive development and to amenity and any harm to the interests of highway safety that may be caused by any phase remaining uncompleted.

name: Condition 5
description: The total amount of floorspace developed shall not exceed 88,524 sq,m (Gross Internal Area) and 100,033 sq.m (Gross External Area).
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the regulatory plans and particulars of the application.

name: Condition 6
description: The amount of floorspace in each respective Development Zone (as indicated on the Regulatory Plans hereby approved) shall not exceed the amount detailed within the following table (Table 1), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority: Table 1: Development Zone Maximum Floorspace GIA (sq.m) Maximum Floorspace GEA (sq.m) A 6343 7145 C 5540 6262 D 19704 (16704*) 22266 (18876*) E 7177 8109 F 9315 10525 G 8238 9310 H 10130 11447 I 12371 13979 J 12726 (9726*) 14380 (10990*) * Maximum Area without basement car parking
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the regulatory plans and particulars of the application.

name: Condition 7
description: The amount of floorspace of each land use hereby approved shall not exceed the amount detailed within the following table (Table 2), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority: Table 2: Land Use or Use Class Maximum Floorspace GIA (sq.m) Maximum Floorspace GEA (sq.m) Residential (Use Class C3) 80630 91112 Business workspace (Use Class B1)* 1010 1140 Mixed Use (Use Class A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, D1, D2) 950 1075 Parking, Plant and Storage 6600 7458 Energy Centre 344 388 *Only in place of Residential (Use Class C3)
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the regulatory plans and particulars of the application.

name: Condition 8
description: The residential accommodation hereby approved shall not exceed 884 units overall, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the regulatory plans and particulars of the application

name: Condition 9
description: Within each Development Zone hereby approved a playable space of at least the area detailed within the following table shall be provided (Table 3), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority: Table 3: Development Zone Minimum Area of Playable Space (sq.m) A 252 C 455 D 245 E 177 F 532 G 450 H 537 I 716 J 685
reason: To ensure that adequate provision is made as part of the development for playable space for children aged from 0 to 11.

name: Condition 10
description: The development shall include at least 400 sqm of floorspace (GEA) for use as Retail (Use Class A1), Financial and professional services (Use Class A2), Restaurants and caf? (Use Class A3), Drinking establishments (Use Class A4), Hot food takeaways (Use Class A5), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. At least 80% of all of the Use Class A floorspace shall be used only for Retail (Use Class A1), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that adequate retail and other service facilities are provided as part of the development for future residents, and to enhance the vitality and viability of any retail floorspace provided.

name: Condition 11
description: The development shall include at least 250 sqm of floorspace (GEA) for use as a community centre (Use Class D1), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that adequate community facilities are provided as part of the development for future residents

name: Condition 12
description: The financial and professional services (Use Class A2) hereby approved shall not be used for the purpose of a betting office, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: In the interest of the general amenity of the area.

name: Condition 13
description: No more than 0.3 car parking spaces per residential units (including disabled car parking spaces) shall be provided, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that adequate car parking is provided for future residents.

name: Condition 14
description: At least 26 disabled car parking spaces shall be provided, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure a socially inclusive and sustainable development and that a reasonable minimum level of parking spaces is provided for use by people with disabilities.

name: Condition 15
description: At least 20% of all car parking spaces shall have electrical charging points, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that a reasonable minimum level of electrical charging points for electrical cars are provided.

name: Condition 16
description: All residential units shall be designed and constructed to achieve Lifetime Homes Standards, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that all residential accommodation is built to a good standard.

name: Condition 17
description: Reserved Matters Applications for each phase shall demonstrate that all of the residential units hereby approved will be designed and constructed as far as practicable to meet the standards contained within the ?Interim London Housing Design Guide? published by the Mayor of London.
reason: To ensure that reasonable living conditions for future occupiers.

name: Condition 18
description: At least 10% of all units shall be built to wheelchair accessible standards or capable of easy adaptation to wheelchair accessible standards, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that adequate accommodation is made for people with disabilities as part of the development.

name: Condition 19
description: All residential accommodation will be provided with private amenity space in the form of a balcony, terrace and/or private garden of at least the following size: 1-bedroom 5 sq.m 2-bedroom 6 sq.m 3-bedroom 8 sq.m 4-bedroom 9 sq.m unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that adequate private amenity space is provided to all new residential units.

name: Condition 20
description: The development hereby approved shall be designed and constructed to meet the minimum design and build standards for security outlined in the ?Secured by Design? (SBD) standards, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the potential for crime and the perception of crime is reduced.

name: Condition 21
description: Prior to the occupation of 370 residential units an Energy Centre shall be provided, and all completed Development Zones shall be connected to the Energy Centre by a District-wide Heat Network and all subsequently completed Development Zones shall be connected to the Energy Centre by a District-wide Heat Network, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the particulars of the application hereby approved and to ensure the efficient provision of energy and heat to all parts of the development.

name: Condition 22
description: No soil stacks, soil vent pipes, flues, ductwork or any other pipework shall be fixed to the street-facing elevations of the buildings hereby approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and does not detract from the character and visual amenity of the area.

name: Condition 23
description: Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, a public realm and landscape management plan, to include long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for all hard and soft landscape areas, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The landscape management plan shall be carried out as approved unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance of the development in maintained.

name: Condition 24
description: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved, a lighting strategy to include details of all lighting to external areas shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure: an appropriate lighting environment is provided to all external areas; light spill is avoided and residential amenity protected, and; a satisfactory appearance of the site.

name: Condition 25
description: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved a feasibility study shall be carried out to assess the potential for moving freight by water during the construction cycle (waste and bulk materials) and following occupation of the development (waste and recyclates). The use of waterborne transport shall be maximised during the construction of the development unless the above assessment demonstrates that such use of the canal is not physically or economically feasible.
reason: To encourage the use of the canal for transporting waste and bulk materials in accordance with Blue Ribbon Network Policies of the London Plan.

name: Condition 26
description: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved a Site Waste Management Plan, detailing the reduction and recycling of demolition and construction waste, The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied.
reason: To ensure that waste from demolition and construction is minimised as par as possible.

name: Condition 27
description: 1. A scheme to maximise the use of sustainable drainage of the site in accordance with the London Plan hierarchy including the following: a. Detailed examination of all roof surfaces to maximise green and brown roofs which in any case should not be less than 50% of the total roof area. b. Detailed examination of all ground /podium surfaces to maximise landscaped areas throughout the development which in any case should not be less than 50% of the courtyard area. c. Detailed examination of all paved areas to maximise permeable surfacing which in any case should not be less than those areas shown to be pedestrianised and for car parking. d. Detailed examination of the ground and context of the site to maximise use of techniques for infiltrating surface water to ground. 2. An overall drainage scheme including the following mitigation measures detailed: a. The phasing of development in conjunction with a drainage design that limits surface water run off for rainfall events up to the 1 in 100 year cc rainfall event to greenfield rates with an acceptable minimum of 5.0l/s from each development zones. b. A drainage design showing containment of surface water to prevent surface flooding up to the 1 in 30 year cc critical rainfall event c. Demonstration by use of drawings and details that surface water runoff can be contained on site to a 1in 100 year cc critical rainfall event and subsequently satisfactorily discharged.
reason: To prevent flooding on site and elsewhere by ensuring the satisfactory storage/disposal of surface water from the site. To ensure surface water runoff is managed maximising the use of sustainable drainage systems and principles and to reduce the volume of run off from the developed site. This condition is supported by PPS25 Para F6 and London Plan policy 5.13. For development zones ?I ? and ?Public Realm? consideration of greenfield run off from the 1 in 1 year and 1 in 30 year rainfall events should also be examined to inform a

name: Condition 28
description: Prior to the commencement of the development a schematic design of the District-wide Heat Network and location of the Energy Centre shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The schematic design should be adhered to in the design of the all phases of development, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the particulars of the application hereby approved and to ensure the efficient provision of energy and heat to all parts of the development.

name: Condition 29
description: Prior to the commencement of the development a Biodiversity Enhancement Plan, including a strategy for habitat enhancements in respect of birds and bat roosting enhancements undertaken in consultation with an suitably qualified ecologist following all necessary further bat surveys has been undertaken shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To enhance the character and ecology of the development in line with Hackney policy and PPS 9.

name: Condition 30
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development full details and samples of all external materials including any window frames, doors, cladding panels, brick work, and/or balconies shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the details as approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the external appearance of the development is satisfactory.

name: Condition 31
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development full details and samples of all ground surface materials and details of any fences, gates of other boundary treatment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the details thus approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that all external areas of the development are of a satisfactory appearance

name: Condition 32
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, a hard and soft landscaping scheme illustrated on detailed drawings, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details shall include: all trees and other planting showing location, species, type of stock, numbers of trees/plants, and areas to be seeded or turfed. All landscaping in accordance with the scheme, when approved, shall be carried out within a period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the development, and shall be maintained to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority for a period of ten years, such maintenance to include the replacement of any plants that die, or are severely damaged, seriously diseased, or removed.
reason: To enhance the character, appearance and ecology of the development and contribution to green infrastructure.

name: Condition 33
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, a tree survey detailing trees to be transplanted and retained, including the methodology for transplanting trees and measures to protect retained trees during demolition and construction, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the details thus approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that any risk of damage to trees during construction is minimised.

name: Condition 34
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, a daylight and sunlight report, detailing the level of daylight and sunlight received by all new residential units, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the design and layout of the residential units allows for adequate daylight and sunlight for the amenity of future occupiers.

name: Condition 35
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, details of the design of all playable space, play equipment and street furniture shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such details as approved shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: In the interest of the visual amenity of the development and wider area, and to meet the needs of future residents.

name: Condition 36
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, full details of the arrangements for storage for refuse and recycling areas shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such details as approved shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To protect the amenity of future residents and to ensure that there is adequate provision for the hygienic and convenient storage of refuse and recycling.

name: Condition 37
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, a detailed layout of any parking area and spaces, including to basements, undercroft or on-street, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. As well as the general layout of the car parking spaces details shall also be provided of: the demarcation of spaces; any signs; any disabled car parking spaces (and to be conveniently located in relation to wheelchair accessible or wheelchair adaptation standard units); electric charging points; the detailed design of any entrance ramps (if within a basement), and the detailed design of any entrance gates (or similar), access controls, or lighting (if within basement or undercroft). Such details as approved shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: In the interests of orderly and satisfactory parking provisions being made on the site to ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or public safety along the adjoining highway.

name: Condition 38
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, details of secure bicycle storage facilities, including layout, stand type and spacing, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such details as approved shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that adequate provision for the safe and secure storage off bicycles is made for occupants and visitors.

name: Condition 39
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, an assessment of the nature and extent of contamination shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This assessment must be undertaken by a competent person, and shall assess any contamination on the site, whether or not it originates on the site. Moreover, it must include: (i) a survey of the extent, scale and nature of contamination; (ii) an assessment of the potential risks to: human health, property (existing or proposed) including buildings, crops, livestock, pets, woodland and service lines and pipes, adjoining land, groundwaters and surface waters, ecological systems, archaeological sites and ancient monuments.
reason: To protect the end user(s) of the development, any adjacent land user(s) and the environment from contamination in line with Planning Policy Statement 23

name: Condition 40
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, a detailed remediation scheme to bring the site to a condition suitable for the intended use by removing unacceptable risks to human health, buildings and other property and the natural and historical environment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme must include all works to be undertaken, proposed remediation objectives and remediation criteria, an appraisal of remedial options, and proposal of the preferred option(s), and a timetable of works and site management procedures. The scheme must ensure that the site will not qualify as contaminated land under Part 2A of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 in relation to the intended use of the land after remediation.
reason: To protect the end user(s) of the development, any adjacent land user(s) and the environment from contamination in line with Planning Policy Statement 23

name: Condition 41
description: The remediation scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved timetable of works. Within 3 months of the completion of measures identified in the approved remediation scheme, a validation report (that demonstrates the effectiveness of the remediation carried out) must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To protect the end user(s) of the development, any adjacent land user(s) and the environment from contamination in line with Planning Policy Statement 23

name: Condition 42
description: In the event that contamination is found at any time when carrying out the approved development that was not previously identified it must be reported in writing within 7 days to the Local Planning Authority and once the Local Planning Authority has identified the part of the site affected by the unexpected contamination development must be halted on that part of the site. An assessment must be undertaken in accordance with the requirements of condition 39, and where remediation is necessary a remediation scheme, together with a timetable for its implementation, must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the requirements of condition 40. The measures in the approved remediation scheme must then be implemented in accordance with the approved timetable. Following completion of measures identified in the approved remediation scheme a validation report must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in accordance with condition 41.
reason: To protect the end user(s) of the development, any adjacent land user(s) and the environment from contamination in line with Planning Policy Statement 23

name: Condition 43
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development, full details of a biodiverse, substrate-based extensive green roof (of variable depth between 80mm and 150mm), to include a detailed maintenance plan, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied.
reason: To enhance the character and ecology of the development, to provide undisturbed refuges for wildlife, to promote sustainable urban drainage, and to enhance the performance and efficiency of the proposed building.

name: Condition 44
description: All residential premises shall be designed in accordance with BS8233:1999 'Sound insulation and noise reduction for buildings-Code of Practice' to attain the following internal noise levels: Criterion Typical situations Design range LAeq, T Good resting conditions Living rooms 30 dB (day: T =16 hours 07:00 ? 23:00) Good sleeping conditions Bedrooms 30 dB (night: T = 8 hours 23:00 ? 07:00) LAmax 45 dB (night 23:00 ? 07:00) Prior to the occupation of any phase of development, a test shall be carried out to show the standard of sound insulation required has been met and the results shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing.
reason: To ensure that the occupiers and users of the proposed development do not suffer a loss of amenity by reason of excess noise from environmental and transportation sources.

name: Condition 45
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development details of the design and location of the relevant part of the District-Wide Heat Network shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the details as approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the particulars of the application hereby approved and to ensure the efficient provision of energy and heat to all parts of the development.

name: Condition 46
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development details of a bat survey, prepared in line with the recommendations of the Bat Survey of Ecology Consulting dated June 2011, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure the development does not impact on protected species.

name: Condition 47
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of the development adjoining the waterway hereby approved a survey of the condition of the waterway wall, and a method statement and schedule of the repairs identified shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any heritage features and materials identified by the survey shall be made available for inspection by British Waterways and where appropriate, preserved in situ or reclaimed and re- used elsewhere on site or on a nearby waterway wall. The repair works identified shall be carried out in accordance with the method statement and repairs schedule by a date to be agreed in the repairs schedule.
reason: In the interest of the structural integrity of the waterway wall, waterway heritage, navigational safety and visual amenity.

name: Condition 48
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of the development adjoining the waterway a Risk Assessment and Method Statement outlining all works to be carried out adjacent to the water shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with British Waterways.
reason: In the interest of the structural integrity of the waterway wall, waterway heritage, navigational safety and visual amenity.

name: Condition 49
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of the development adjoining the waterway full details of a specific waterways landscaping scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with British Waterways. The landscaping scheme should include reference to plant species types, surface treatments, fences and walls, any signage and information boards together with the means of on-going maintenance for a five year period. The approved landscaping scheme shall be implemented by the first planting scheme after the development commences.
reason: In the interest of preserving open views to and from the canal, the living environment for future residents and the canal setting.

name: Condition 50
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of the development adjoining the waterway, full details of any proposed lighting and CCTV scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with British Waterways. The approved lighting and CCTV scheme should be implemented prior to first occupation of the relevant part of the development.
reason: In the interest of crime prevention, ecology, visual amenity and the canal setting.

name: Condition 51
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of the development adjoining the waterway, an assessment of potential biodiversity impacts of any proposed canal access and or ?canal walkway? shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied.
reason: To conserve and enhance the wildlife value of the canal in line with Core Strategy Policies 27 and 28 and the Mayors Biodiversity Strategy.

name: Condition 52
description: Prior to the commencement of any development within Development Zone D hereby approved, a detailed wind assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The wind assessment shall provide details of the wind micro-climate conditions at building entrances and to relevant locations of open space and amenity space adjacent to the development and in the vicinity of the site and set out any mitigation measures to be required. Any mitigation measures shall be implemented in full and retained as such, unless otherwise in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the wind micro-climate does not adversely impact on the amenity of the immediate surroundings.

name: Condition 53
description: Prior to the commencement of any phase of development which contains a use falling within Use Class A1, A2, A3, A4, or A5 (as defined by the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended)) details of the design of the shopfront and location, type and size of signage shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the details thus approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that the external appearance of the development is satisfactory.

name: Condition 54
description: No Use Class A3 or A5 use shall commence on site until detailed plans and specification of the appearance of and the equipment comprising an extract ventilation system which shall include measures to alleviate noise, vibration, fumes and odours (and incorporating active carbon filters, silencer(s), and anti vibration mountings where necessary) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. After the system has been approved, it shall be installed in accordance with the approved plans and specification before any Use Class A3 or A5 use is implemented, and shall thereafter be permanently maintained in accordance with the approved specification.
reason: In the interest of adjoining residential amenity

name: Condition 55
description: i) The rating level of the noise emitted from the energy centre on the site shall be 10dB below the existing background level at any time. The noise levels shall be determined at the facade of any noise sensitive property. The measurements and assessments shall be made according to BS4142:1997. ii) Development (of the relevant phase) shall not commence until details of a scheme complying with paragraph (i) of this condition have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. iii) The development (of the relevant phase) shall not be occupied until the scheme approved pursuant to paragraph (ii) of this condition has been implemented in its entirety. Thereafter, the scheme shall be maintained in perpetuity unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: In the interest of adjoining residential amenity

name: Condition 56
description: Prior to the commencement of Development Zone E, details of the design of the Energy Centre shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the details as approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with the particulars of the application hereby approved and to ensure the efficient provision of energy and heat to all parts of the development.

name: Condition 57
description: Prior to the commencement of of any development within Zone C full details of a replacement bus layover and bus turnaround scheme (including any temporary arrangements during construction) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme as approved shall be implemented in full and retained as such prior to the commencement of any development within Zone C, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
reason: To ensure that suitable bus layover and turning facilities are continuously provided in this vicinity in order to support the efficient operation of the bus network and in accordance with London Plan policy 6.2 and the Land for Transport SPG.

name: Condition 1
description: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.
reason: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended.

name: Condition 2
description: The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.
reason: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

name: Condition 3
description: All new external finishes in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works to be carried out in this connection) shall match the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution and finished appearance.
reason: To ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and does not detract from the character and visual amenity of the area.

name: Condition 4
description: No development shall commence, other than works of demolition, until a detailed specification and a drainage layout of at least one suitable sustainable drainage systems (i.e. water butt, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof (substrate depth of 80-150mm excluding the vegetative mat), permeable paving etc.) has been submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the SuDS officer. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume for all return periods up to the 1 in 100 year storm events plus an allowance for climate change.
reason: In the interests of prevention of exacerbation of surface water flood risk to adjoining land.

name: Condition 5
description: The roof of the extension shall not be used for any purpose other than as a means of escape in emergency or for maintenance of the building. In particular the roof shall not be used as a roof terrace, balcony or any other amenity area.
reason: To safeguard the amenities of the adjoining premises and the area generally.
